BiblicalUsage: Chalaph in Aramaic means for time to pass on. All four times it falls in Nebuchadnezzar's sentence: let his heart be changed and let seven times pass over him, till seven times pass over him, until seven times pass over him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe seven times passing over a king is God's clock, not man's: the grass eats the king until the king learns who rules, and the times pass only when God says they have passed enough. Seven times is not a sentence without an end — it ends when the king lifts his eyes to heaven.
